title: Deciphering the regulatory landscape of untranslated regions across cell types
text:
Gene expression regulation by mRNA untranslated regions (UTRs) is essential for numerous cellular processes,
and its dysregulation disrupts development and causes many human diseases. Despite this importance, we lack
a comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms and sequence determinants underlying UTR
regulation, especially regarding cell type-specificity. To address this gap, I propose three aims: 1) investigate the
mechanistic basis of cell type-specific UTR regulation through targeted experiments; 2) systematically map RNA-
binding proteins that interact with UTRs; and 3) develop a machine learning model to predict the functional effects
of genetic variants in UTRs.

title: Transcriptional Responses to Wildfire Pollution in Airway Epithelial Cells Identify Genetic Risk Factors and Mechanisms of Asthma Exacerbations
text:
Asthma exacerbations are responsible for the major health impacts associated with the disease, and increased
air pollution from wildfire smoke is a major contributor to exacerbations. Patients with asthma experience
variable sensitivity to air pollution, and public health recommendations fail to appropriately target high risk
patients. Using primary human tissue culture, next-generation sequencing-based techniques and bioinformatic
tools, we will characterize genetic risk factors that connect wildfire air pollution with asthma exacerbations and
identify mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets for pollution-associated asthma exacerbations.

title: Understanding Mechanisms of Organic Reactions and Processes through Imaging
text:
The new imaging methods that will result from the proposed research are relevant to public health because they
provide fundamental information that enables the efficient and sustainable preparation of compounds for drug
discovery. The fundamental insight from these studies is relevant to NIGMS’s mission because the increased
accessibility of these pharmaceutical candidates lays the foundation for advances in disease treatment.

title: Digging for Novel Neuropeptides: Identification and characterization of neuropeptides and their receptors in the earthworm, Dendrobaena veneta
text:
Neuropeptides released from neurons regulate almost every aspect of animal physiology and are
reciprocally active across phyla; studying them can inform our fundamental understanding of these molecules,
and characterizing their unique features in other animals can transform our understanding of human diseases
where neuropeptides are known to play a role. For the proposed project, we will identify and characterize
neuropeptides that regulate physiological functions in earthworms in order to pinpoint the unique modifications
to the genes responsible for neuropeptide signaling. We suspect that earthworms will possess unique
modifications to these genes that do not exist elsewhere because earthworm genomes have undergone a
recent and profoundly chaotic rearrangement absent in more commonly studied organisms. Funding for this
project will have a transformative effect on training opportunities for students and the overall biomedical
research environment at Kean University in Union, NJ.

title: Novel AAV gene therapy for treating CNS neuropathy of MPS IIIC
text:
MPS IIIC is a devastating lysosomal storage disease (LSD), for which no treatment is currently available. Target
the root cause, this project is to develop an effective gene replacement therapy product for treating MPS IIIC,
using AAV9 vector with signals to facilitate mRNA packaging in extracellular vesicles (EVs) that can facilitate by-
stander-effect and cross-correction. The goal of this Phase I STTR is to generate pre-clinical data to support the
further development towards clinical application and commercialization.

title: Coronary Endothelial Cell Dysfunction in Diabetes: Role of MFGE8
text:
More than 37 million people in the United States have diabetes. Despite many medications for diabetes,
the number of deaths resulting from coronary vascular complications, including coronary microvascular
disease, is still high among patients with diabetes. This study is designed to identify the cellular defects
that cause the abnormalities of small coronary arteries in diabetic patients and to develop new therapeutic
approaches for coronary endothelial dysfunction in diabetes.

title: Role of ELOVL2 in age-related visual decline
text:
The retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) is critical in preserving healthy vision, and degeneration of the RPE can
lead to irreversible blindness. This project will investigate the basic biology of the RPE, its role in maintaining
the health of the retina, and how essential processes are affected during aging. Understanding the molecular
underpinnings of age- and disease-related changes in the RPE will inform the development of therapeutics to
combat blinding diseases.

title: Molecularly Engineered Lectins for Intranasal Prophylaxis and Treatment of Coronaviruses
text:
The present crisis caused by SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) has harshly illuminated the ability of coronavirus
pandemics to sicken and kill millions of individuals, ruin large parts of the economy, and to lead to great social
stress. Vaccines, oral and systemic medications, and monoclonal antibodies have all proven effective against
SARS-CoV-2, but each has encountered problems with uptake and/or viral and societal resistance, and there
is presently no drug on the market with pan-coronavirus activity that would anticipate SARS-CoV-2 evolution
and outbreaks of new and deadly coronavirus infections. We have used targeted molecular engineering of a
lectin (sugar-binding protein) to create a new broad-spectrum, well-tolerated antiviral agent with significant
activity against all coronaviruses tested, including SARS-CoV-2 and variants such as Omicron, and here
propose studies that will lead to the effective clinical implementation of intranasal use of this new agent to
prevent and treat infection with SARS-CoV-2, diverse coronaviruses, and also ultimately influenza.

title: IDENTIFYING THE EFFECTS OF SOCIALLY RELATED STRESS ON STRESS REACTIVITY AND CRAVING IN INDIVIDUALS WITH ALCOHOL USE DISORDER
text: Social stress (SS) is related to increased risk for alcohol use disorder (AUD). Understanding how SS affects alcohol use and the risk of developing AUD can inform more effective, tailored interventions. This project uses a human laboratory paradigm and ecological momentary assessment (EMA) to examine the effects of SS on cue-induced stress and craving, and to evaluate the role of individual-level factors in shaping these responses. Findings will inform strategies to improve AUD treatment outcomes.

title: Determining how Sox9 taste progenitors are established embryonically and contribute adult taste buds
text:
Cancer patients undergoing chemo- or radiotherapy often experience alteration or loss of taste function, which
can impact their quality of life and prognosis outcomes. Therefore, understanding how taste is maintained
under homeostasis provides a critical foundation for the development of therapies to treat taste dysfunction.
The circumvallate papilla is an ideal model to study this, as it comprises hundreds of taste buds; this proposal
seeks to understand CVP homeostasis by understanding when taste stems arise during development and how
they contribute to taste buds in adults.

title: Genetic Recombination and Genome Rearrangements
text:
The FASEB conference on Genetic Recombination and Genome Rearrangements brings together the world’s
leading researchers investigating the mechanisms and regulation of genetic recombination and chromosome
rearrangements. This field encompasses several topics directly relevant to the biology of cancer, aging, cell
senescence, telomere maintenance, as well as to the mechanisms promoting age-related disease. Therefore,
a mechanistic understanding of these processes is paramount for an improved understanding of cancer
etiology, premature aging, for the identification of critical biomarkers of these conditions, and for developing
novel strategies for therapy.

title: Development and Translation of D-glucose as a Diagnostic Agent for MRI of Cancer
text:
Annually, about 50,000,000 doses of synthetic gadolinium imaging contrast agents are injected into
patients worldwide when getting an MRI scan. While these agents are extremely safe, they have the
potential for adverse effects in some patient populations, which may accumulate when a procedure is
repeated. We propose to develop the use of sugar (D-glucose) as a biodegradable contrast agent for
imaging tumor physiology with MRI; we will first develop and translate this approach for brain cancer,
after which the technology can be adjusted for use in other cancers and other disorders.

title: SLC24A4 in enamel maturation, from expression to etiology
text:
Tooth enamel is the hardest tissue in the human body and requires the calcium transporter SLC24A4 (solute
carrier family 24, member 4) to achieve its high degree of mineralization. Mutations in SLC24A4 cause
amelogenesis imperfecta, a congenital enamel defect disorder that decreases quality of life due to the continuous
risk of tooth fracture, chronic pain, and increased dental decay. In order to elucidate new strategies to regenerate
enamel and treat patients with amelogenesis imperfecta, this proposal aims to utilize powerful genomic,
biochemical, cell biological, and imaging approaches to understand how SLC24A4 is transcriptionally regulated
in normal enamel development and how the enamel-forming cells are disrupted when SLC24A4 is mutated.

title: Ferroptosis and Polyunsaturated Fatty Acid Metabolism
text:
Our investigation of the crosstalk between ferroptosis and polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolism will lead to a
better understanding of the role of polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolites in programmed cell death that will have
huge implications on human physiology and may identify novel treatments for many diseases. Specifically, we
will combine synthetic metabolites and mimics as powerful chemical probes, state-of-the-art analytical tools,
genetic tools, and a novel model organism to delineate how polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolites regulate
ferroptosis. Our preliminary data and data from others suggest that specific polyunsaturated fatty acids trigger
ferroptosis and inhibition of polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolism rescues ferroptosis triggered by specific
polyunsaturated fatty acids illustrating that particular polyunsaturated fatty acids or their metabolites could have
a major role in ferroptosis.

title: Excitation and Inhibition in Neural Circuits of the Visual Cortex
text:
How excitatory and inhibitory circuits mediate neural computation in the cerebral cortex is central to
understanding vision, and brain function more generally. Disruptions of the precise balance between excitation
and inhibition in the cerebral cortex can lead to a variety of neurological disorders. Thus, understanding how
excitatory and inhibitory circuits drive sensory perception should help reveal the underlying causes of certain
neurological diseases.

title: Leveraging redox dysregulation to advance DIPG treatment strategies
text:
Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) is a fatal childhood cancer of the brainstem with radiation therapy as the
only treatment option. Thus, novel therapies able to overcome therapeutic resistance and enhance sensitization
of DIPG tumors to radiation without causing additional side effects are desperately needed. To improve the
overall survival of DIPG patients, I propose to investigate the selective therapeutic agents, auranofin and Cu-
ATSM, in combination with radiation and will evaluate their mechanism of cell killing in DIPG tumors.

title: Characterizing epistasis in yeast using CRISPR and chromosome synthesis
text:
Epistasis causes genetic variants to exhibit different effects depending on the genotypic
contexts in which they occur. This context dependence makes it hard to achieve a predictive
understanding of the relationship between individuals’ genomes and traits. We will improve
understanding of epistasis by (1) studying how epistasis causes CRISPR perturbations to show
different effects in distinct individuals and (2) using chromosome synthesis to characterize the
extent of epistasis between related taxa.

title: Novel mouse models of hepatitis B virus infection and replication
text:
Hepatitis B virus (HBV) chronically infects about 250 million people with annual 1 million deaths worldwide. The
search for a cure of chronic hepatitis B has been hampered by the lack of small animal models of HBV
infection and replication. The overall goal of this application is to develop murine models of HBV infection and
replication for the study of HBV infection, replication, pathogenesis, and carcinogenesis. More importantly,
murine models of HBV infection will foster discovery and development of more effective antiviral drugs towards
a cure of chronic hepatitis B.

title: Genetic architecture of age of onset of amyloid positivity: Integrating imaging and genetic tools to identify novel drivers of disease
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE.
Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the sixth leading cause of death in the United States, affecting almost 6 million
people which is expected to more than double by mid-century. The neuropathologic hallmarks of AD including
β-amyloid (Aβ) plaques and tau neurofibrillary tangles accumulate in the brain decades before symptom
onset, and drive downstream neurodegeneration, cognitive impairment, and death. Identifying genetic drivers
of early neuropathologic changes like conversion to Aβ positivity (Aβ+) may lead to novel therapeutic targets
useful earlier in the disease cascade when treatment is most effective.

title: Advanced PET Quantitative Reconstruction and Deep Learning Noise Reduction Algorithms for Receptor Occupancy Studies on Ultra-High-Performance Brain PET Systems
text:
This research is highly relevant to public health as it aims to develop advanced PET reconstruction and kinetic
modeling techniques, which are crucial for accurate drug efficacy assessments in central nervous system
(CNS) disorders. By enhancing the precision and efficiency of high-resolution PET receptor occupancy studies,
this work will facilitate the development of more effective treatments for neurological diseases. Improved PET
kinetic parameter estimation capabilities will ultimately lead to better clinical outcomes and improved quality of
life for patients affected by CNS disorders.
